source_name: Tatra banka — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: RBI subsidiary, ~3,500 staff, strongest digital/innovation employer brand in SK. Its page is where Tatra banka announces new board members, innovation-unit leads and hiring waves (Tatra banka Digital/Elevate).

source_name: 365.bank — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Mid-size retail bank (~616 staff) undergoing ownership change (KBC-linked consolidation). Ownership transitions produce the densest cluster of leadership-move and reorg posts, both on the page and from departing/arriving staff.

source_name: ČSOB Finančná skupina — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: KBC-owned SK universal bank; page publishes management-board appointments and group-level reorganisation news relevant to both banking and payments workstreams.

source_name: Komerční banka Slovakia — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Small SK branch operation; low headcount means individual hires are visible as discrete signals, and the page shows corporate-banking staffing intent in SK.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Central bank / supervisor. Its page announces senior supervisory and payment-systems appointments and recruits; NBS staff moving into commercial banks (and vice versa) is a recurring SK talent flow worth tracking person-side.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (Slovak Banking Association) — LinkedIn page
why_relevant: Sector body whose page reposts member-bank leadership announcements and names working-group chairs — an efficient pointer to which individuals hold payments/regulatory portfolios at each member bank.

source_name: TrustPay — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Bratislava-headquartered licensed payment institution (est. 2009) with cross-border acquiring. Its LinkedIn page and staff posts are the fastest indicator of SK payments-sector hiring, compliance-team build-out and commercial leadership changes.

source_name: Besteron — LinkedIn company page and founder/exec profiles
why_relevant: SK payment-gateway provider (Bratislava, 11-50 staff). Small-team payments firms announce every senior hire personally; an individual profile such as Ivan Duliak surfaced directly in search, confirming person-centric discoverability for this cell.

source_name: K-Pay a.s. — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Smaller SK payments actor surfaced by an English payments-hiring query; useful for completing the payments-side actor map beyond the well-known names.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. executive profiles (regional card-processing hub)
why_relevant: Bankart is a regional card/payment processor serving CEE banks; its management-board announcements are made on personal profiles first. Demonstrates the cell's core hypothesis (person announces before employer) and covers processor-side org change affecting SK issuers.

source_name: Pedersen & Partners Bratislava — executive search consultant posts
why_relevant: Executive search firm active in SK financial services since 2003. Consultants publish placement announcements on LinkedIn, and the firm's own site lists the consultants whose feeds should be watched — recruiters often post a placement before the employer's press release.

source_name: Amrop Slovakia — executive search / leadership advisory
why_relevant: 30+ years in SK leadership search; frequently mandated for bank board and C-level roles. Consultant LinkedIn posts and firm insight pieces flag both completed placements and which banks are running searches.

source_name: KPMG Slovakia Executive Search
why_relevant: Big-four talent arm placing mid-to-executive financial roles in SK; its market commentary and consultant posts indirectly reveal banking demand pockets (risk, compliance, payments product).

source_name: KiTalent — Bratislava executive search with continuous talent mapping
why_relevant: Claims continuous talent mapping across Bratislava financial services — i.e. it maintains exactly the person-level org map this cell wants, and publishes fragments of it as marketing content.

source_name: CEE Chamber — top recruitment companies in Slovakia (pointer list)
why_relevant: Aggregated list naming SK recruiters (Pro HR, PERSONALITY and others) — a cheap way to snowball the recruiter watchlist beyond the internationally visible brands, which matters because local boutiques handle much of the mid-level banking movement.

source_name: Startitup.sk — banking leadership-change reporting
why_relevant: Demonstrated concrete SK-language coverage of bank board changes (UniCredit CZ/SK new CEO; Privatbanka board strengthening), naming individuals whose LinkedIn profiles then become watchlist entries.

source_name: Forbes Slovensko — LinkedIn / labour-market and executive coverage
why_relevant: Forbes SK covers both executive changes (e.g. Profesia CEO succession) and LinkedIn-derived labour-market data for Slovakia, giving a bridge between the person-centric channel and quantified hiring trends.

source_name: Alma Career Slovakia (Profesia) — LinkedIn page and showcase pages
why_relevant: Operator of Profesia.sk; its LinkedIn page and 'Senior pracovné ponuky' showcase page push senior SK vacancies (including banking) into the professional-social channel, and its own leadership changed recently — a marker of the SK labour-data ecosystem.

source_name: RocketReach company profiles for SK banking entities (headcount proxy)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator that mirrors LinkedIn-derived employee counts and executive names, usable as a headcount-trend proxy where LinkedIn itself cannot be automated. Accuracy is uneven, so treat as a corroborating signal only.

source_name: Aeroleads — Top payments companies in Slovakia (actor-map pointer)
why_relevant: Enumerates ~22 SK payments companies, giving a ready candidate list of LinkedIn company pages to add to the monitoring set for the payments half of the cell.

source_name: Amrop Slovakia – News & Insights
why_relevant: Largest executive search firm in Slovakia by filled senior positions; publishes market commentary, leadership-succession insight and placement/ranking news that signals which C-level functions banks are building.

source_name: Amrop Slovensko legacy site – articles (amrop.sk)
why_relevant: Older Slovak-language article archive of Amrop SK with thought-leadership on management hiring practices; useful for historical baseline of search-firm commentary.

source_name: Stanton Chase – Financial Services / FinTech practice
why_relevant: Global retained search firm covering CEE financial services and fintech; publishes sector leadership reports and consultant commentary. SK mandates appear to be served from regional offices (Prague/Vienna) rather than a confirmed Bratislava office.

source_name: Hays Slovakia employer profile on Profesia.sk
why_relevant: Live listing of roles Hays Slovakia is mandated to fill, including its Hays Banking and Hays Finance & Accounting divisions — a direct read on which banking/payments functions are being staffed via intermediaries.

source_name: Hays Salary Guide / Mzdový průzkum (CZ-SK regional)
why_relevant: Annual salary benchmark covering ~400 roles across 12 specializations incl. banking and finance; the CZ entity also covers Slovak/CEE business-services and banking recruitment, so it is the accessible proxy for Hays SK benchmarks.

source_name: Grafton Slovakia – Mediálna zóna / tlačové správy
why_relevant: Grafton runs the largest Slovak private-sector salary survey (360 positions across 8 industries, regional breakdowns) and issues frequent press releases on candidate behaviour, offer-rejection rates and scarce skills — a leading indicator of talent tightness in finance/IT.

source_name: Gi Group Slovakia (parent of Grafton SK) – insights
why_relevant: Parent group republishes and extends Grafton's SK labour-market analysis; sometimes carries commentary not on grafton.sk.

source_name: ManpowerGroup Slovensko – Index trhu práce (MEOS)
why_relevant: Quarterly employer hiring-intent survey with sector cuts (incl. finance/real-estate); Slovakia has been in the panel since 2011, giving a long comparable series on net hiring outlook — a leading indicator of headcount plans at banks.
